backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=3, class_weight='balanced_subsample', and N_TREES=500 in the random forest to give smoother probabilities and better ranking.
backlog.title: RF with min_samples_leaf 3 and balanced class weight

backlog.spec: Variance from a single fit is a real part of the loss on 1624 molecules. Wrap both the RF and the LGBM in a loop over 3 derived seeds (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000), rank-transform each model's test probabilities, and average all 6 rank vectors equally for the final prediction. Reduce N_TREES to 200 per RF fit so the total runtime stays near the current budget. Nothing else changes; this is a pure variance-reduction change and should give a small but reliable improvement.
backlog.title: Bag each model over several seeds

backlog.spec: Change the RandomForestClassifier to n_estimators=1000 and max_features='sqrt' (keep min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed). With roughly 2250 columns, max_features=0.3 means each split considers about 675 correlated features, which makes the trees nearly deterministic and highly correlated with each other; 'sqrt' gives about 47, decorrelating the ensemble, and the larger forest absorbs the extra variance that introduces. The baseline job takes ~33 s and the incumbent is well inside the 10-minute cap, so 1000 trees is affordable. Leave the LightGBM member and the equal-weight rank blend exactly as they are.
backlog.title: Retune the random forest: more trees, sqrt feature draw

backlog.spec: Change the RF to MAX_FEATURES=0.15 and max_depth=20, with min_samples_leaf=2. The aim is a more decorrelated forest on the larger descriptor-augmented feature set.
backlog.title: RF max_features tuning with depth cap

backlog.spec: Replace the single Morgan generator with three generators built once at module level: Morgan radius 2 (2048 bits, standard invariants), Morgan radius 3 (2048 bits, standard invariants), and a feature-based Morgan (FCFP-like) radius 2 with 1024 bits created via rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=1024, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Concatenate all three bit vectors with the 11 hand descriptors in featurize. FCFP abstracts atoms into donor/acceptor/aromatic/halogen roles, which generalises better across unseen scaffolds than exact atom identity. No model changes.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan union of radius 2 and 3 plus pharmacophore-style FCFP

backlog.spec: Blood-brain-barrier datasets contain salts, mixtures and charged forms that make otherwise identical molecules look different. In featurize and full_descriptors, pre-process each SMILES: parse, keep only the largest fragment by heavy atom count (split on '.' or use rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True), run Chem.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger on it, and then compute fingerprints and descriptors on the cleaned molecule. Cache the cleaned molecule by input SMILES so the work is done once. If parsing or standardisation fails, fall back to the original molecule, and if that also fails emit a zero vector. No model changes.
backlog.title: Standardise and de-salt SMILES before featurising

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.5 and 0.5 rank-average with a weight w chosen from {0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8} for the RF member (1 minus w for LightGBM). Choose w inside fit_predict with a 3-fold GroupKFold over Murcko scaffolds computed from train_smiles, maximising the mean ROC AUC of the weighted rank blend on the held-out inner folds. Use the seed for any randomness and fit the final RF and LightGBM on all training rows with the chosen w. Keep the member models and their settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Blend weight chosen by inner scaffold CV

backlog.spec: Add an ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features 0.3, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) trained on the same features, and include its scaled rank prediction in the average with the RF and LGBM predictions (equal weights).
backlog.title: Add ExtraTrees to ensemble

backlog.spec: Replace the binary Morgan bit vector in featurize() with a count vector: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy(mol), keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits. Counts of each substructure carry more information than presence/absence, and the random forest and LightGBM can split on them directly. Leave the descriptors, clipping and the two-model rank average unchanged.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add a small block of hand-written SMARTS count features computed per molecule and appended to the feature matrix: carboxylic acid [CX3](=O)[OX2H1,OX1-], other acidic groups (tetrazole, sulfonic acid, phosphate), primary and secondary/tertiary aliphatic amines ([NX3;!$(N-C=[O,N,S]);!$(N-a)]), quaternary ammonium [N+;!$(N=*);!$(N-[O-])], amide C(=O)N, hydroxyl [OX2H], halogens, nitro, and sulfonamide. Also add ratios TPSA/MolWt, (HBD+HBA)/HeavyAtoms and a count of formally charged atoms. Compute each with Chem.MolFromSmarts and len(mol.GetSubstructMatches(patt)). These encode the acid, base and polarity rules known to govern blood-brain barrier passage.
backlog.title: BBB-domain pharmacophore count features

backlog.spec: Augment the hand descriptor list in `descriptors` with quantities known to drive passive brain penetration, computed from values already available: logP minus TPSA/25 (a crude CNS MPO-like term), TPSA divided by molecular weight, number of hydrogen bond donors plus acceptors, Crippen molar refractivity (Crippen.MolMR), Descriptors.NumAromaticHeterocycles, Descriptors.NHOHCount, Descriptors.NOCount, the count of basic nitrogens (aliphatic N not in an amide or aromatic ring) and a binary flag for any formal charge. Append these after the existing 11 values. Keep the fingerprints, the full descriptor block and both models unchanged; the goal is to give the trees a few strong, low-noise axes to split on early.
backlog.title: Add physicochemical BBB-relevant derived descriptors

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, remove the Morgan fingerprint columns from X_train/X_test and use only the full RDKit descriptor matrix (clipped). BBB penetration is largely driven by physchem properties (TPSA, HBD, logP, charge), and with scaffold-split folds fingerprint bits may add noise. Keep the RF + LGBM rank ensemble.
backlog.title: Drop Morgan bits, use descriptors only

backlog.spec: Instead of hard-coding equal weights, learn the blend inside fit_predict. Run a StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training set, collect out-of-fold probabilities for the RF and the LGBM, rank-transform each OOF column, then fit a small LogisticRegression on those two columns against y. Refit both base models on the full training set, rank-transform their test predictions, and apply the learned logistic weights to produce the final probability. Guard against a degenerate fit by falling back to the 0.5/0.5 average if the learned coefficients are not both positive. Keep total runtime under control by using N_TREES=200 inside the OOF loop.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold stacking blend weights instead of a fixed 50/50

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM member's hyperparameters with a slower and longer schedule: n_estimators=1500, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, min_child_samples=20, keeping random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. The current 300 rounds at lr 0.05 with no row subsampling is a fairly aggressive fit for 1300 training molecules; trading step size for rounds and adding per-iteration bagging is the standard way to buy a small amount of accuracy on tabular data of this size. Check that the job still fits the 10-minute budget for all 15 fits. The random forest member and the rank-average blend are unchanged.
backlog.title: Slower, longer, row-subsampled LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a linear member: standardize the non-fingerprint feature columns (the 11 descriptors and the full RDKit descriptor block, after the existing percentile clipping) with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold, leave the binary fingerprint bits as is, and fit LogisticRegression(C=0.1, penalty='l2', max_iter=2000, solver='liblinear', random_state=seed). Rank-average its test probabilities with the RF and LightGBM ranks, each at weight one-third. Linear models on physicochemical descriptors are a strong baseline for BBB permeability and add diversity to the tree ensemble.
backlog.title: Regularized logistic regression member

backlog.spec: Add a pipeline of QuantileTransformer (normal output) then LogisticRegression (C=0.1, max_iter=2000) on the clipped full descriptors only, and add its scaled rank prediction with weight 1/3 alongside the RF and LGBM. This adds a smooth, low-variance linear model.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on scaled descriptors in ensemble

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute a non-isomeric canonical SMILES for every training and test molecule with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, isomericSmiles=False) after Chem.MolFromSmiles. For each test molecule whose key appears among training keys, replace its model score with a blended value: 0.5 times the model rank score plus 0.5 times the mean training label for that key, both on the [0, 1] scale. Test molecules with no match keep the pure blended score. This handles stereoisomer and salt-free duplicates that the scaffold split may place in the same fold. Keep the models unchanged.
backlog.title: Canonical non-isomeric SMILES label lookup

backlog.spec: Keep the random forest and the existing LightGBM, and add a third rank-averaged member: a second LGBMClassifier with deliberately different capacity and feature sampling, e.g. n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=63, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.7, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed + 1, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1, fitted on the same full matrix. Return the equal-weight mean of the three scaled_rank vectors. Previous third members failed because they were weak or structurally unlike the winners (logistic regression, MLP, kNN); here the new member is from the family that already works, and the gain, if any, comes from decorrelating two boosters that disagree about depth and feature fraction.
backlog.title: Add a second, differently tuned LightGBM to the blend

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the column sums of the Morgan bit block (the first 2048 columns) on X_train. Keep only the bits that are on in at least 10 training molecules. Apply the same column mask to X_test, and keep all the descriptor columns. Fit RF and LightGBM on the reduced matrix.
backlog.title: Drop rare Morgan bits

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, before any featurization or descriptor computation, map every SMILES (train and test) to its largest fragment by heavy-atom count: mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(s); frags = Chem.GetMolFrags(mol, asMols=True); keep max(frags, key=lambda m: m.GetNumHeavyAtoms()). Optionally neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Use the cleaned molecules for the Morgan features, the 11 hand-picked descriptors, the full RDKit descriptor list and the _DESC_CACHE key (key on the cleaned SMILES). Keep everything else unchanged. Counter-ions and salts in BBBP otherwise distort MolWt, TPSA and the charge count.
backlog.title: Largest-fragment salt stripping before featurization

backlog.spec: Switch the Morgan block from binary bits to counts: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy, then apply np.log1p to that block so that large counts do not dominate the distance-free tree splits. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits, keep everything else (hand descriptors, full descriptor clipping, RF and LGBM settings, rank averaging) identical. Counts carry multiplicity information that binary bits discard and often help gradient boosting more than random forests, so report the per-model behaviour if easy.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan features with log1p scaling

backlog.spec: Replace the equal 0.5/0.5 rank average with a 0.4 RF / 0.6 LightGBM weighting. Change nothing else, so this tests the blend weight.
backlog.title: Weighted blend favouring the stronger member

backlog.spec: Add a third rank-averaged member: a RandomForest (300 trees, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=2) trained only on the clipped full RDKit descriptor columns, with no fingerprint bits. Give it a blend weight of 1/3.
backlog.title: Test-time descriptor-only RF member

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold SMILES of each training molecule with MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles. Set the sample weight to 1/sqrt(count of that scaffold in the training set). Normalise the weights to mean 1 and pass them to the RF and LightGBM fit calls through sample_weight. This reduces the dominance of large congeneric series.
backlog.title: Sample weights by inverse scaffold frequency

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, try a small grid for the RandomForestClassifier only: max_features in {sqrt(n_features), 0.15, 0.3} and min_samples_leaf in {1, 3, 5}. Score each pair with a 3-fold GroupKFold over Murcko scaffold ids of train_smiles, using mean ROC AUC on the held-out inner folds, and fit the final forest with the best pair on all training rows with n_estimators=N_TREES and random_state=seed. Keep LightGBM and the rank-average blend as they are. Set n_jobs=8 to stay within the time limit.
backlog.title: Random forest hyperparameter sweep with inner group CV

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the single RandomForestClassifier with an average of 3 forests of 300 trees each, using seeds seed, seed+1 and seed+2. Average their predict_proba outputs before rank scaling. Keep the LightGBM member unchanged. This is meant to cut the variance of the forest member.
backlog.title: Multi-seed RF averaging

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after building the clipped descriptor matrix from the training fold, remove redundant columns: first drop any column with zero variance on the training fold, then compute the correlation matrix of the remainder and, scanning columns in order, drop any column whose absolute Pearson correlation with an already-kept column exceeds 0.95. Apply the identical kept-column index set to the test matrix. The descList contains many near-duplicates (several molecular-weight variants, nested Chi and Kappa families, counts that are linear in heavy-atom count); pruning them raises the share of informative columns in each random max_features or colsample draw without discarding any real signal. Fit the selection on training-fold data only, never on test.
backlog.title: Drop near-duplicate descriptor columns

backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 3 in the RandomForest so its probabilities are smoother. Leave everything else unchanged. The rank blend should gain from less noisy forest scores.
backlog.title: Larger RF min_samples_leaf

backlog.spec: Keep featurize and the full descriptor block as they are, but change the Morgan generator to fpSize=512 bits at radius 2 (set N_BITS = 512). Leave the RF and LightGBM hyperparameters unchanged so the only change is the fingerprint width. The intent is that the descriptors carry most of the signal and fewer, less sparse Morgan columns reduce noise on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Smaller Morgan fold with the full descriptor set

backlog.spec: Change N_BITS from 2048 to 512, leaving radius 2, both models, the 11 physchem descriptors and the clipped descList untouched. Evidence so far says the descriptors, not the fingerprint, carry the signal: every fingerprint swap or addition tested has been neutral or worse, while descriptor blocks produced both accepted gains. A 2048-bit sparse block diluting a ~210-column descriptor block means both the forest's max_features=0.3 draw and LightGBM's colsample_bytree=0.3 draw mostly sample near-empty bit columns. Folding the same structural information into 512 bins raises the chance that each tree split candidate set contains an informative descriptor, and it also cuts fit time.
backlog.title: Shrink the Morgan block to 512 bits

memo: Helped: the RF+LightGBM blend (0.1194 vs baseline ~0.1361) and appending RDKit descriptors (11 physchem 0.1040; full descList 0.0944 and 0.0842, incumbent mean_adjusted 0.0893 over 2 runs). Descriptors drive the gain. Did not help: other fingerprint swaps or additions (atom-pair 0.0949, MACCS 0.0921, Morgan counts 0.0940, BRICS 0.0938), model swaps (XGBoost 0.1041, CatBoost 0.0950, ExtraTrees 0.0948, SVC 0.1255), LightGBM variants (DART 0.0967, regularized 0.0958, monotone 0.0942), and extra members like LR or MLP. Tanimoto kNN (0.0884), label spreading (0.0896), torsion counts (0.0902) and LR stacking (0.0900) were within noise. The two incumbent runs differ by about 0.01, twice the noise sd of ~0.0049, so single-run deltas under 0.01 are unreliable. Next: replicate the incumbent and the kNN variant to firm up the baseline. Tune blend weights and tree hyperparameters on the descriptors. Try fewer fingerprint bits. Avoid more fingerprint swaps, kernel models and model-family swaps.
